After each camp, at some point in the morning, everything you need to live fits together nicely in one package, which has two wheels.

Scroll back on my https://t.me/s/tour2020 to about March 1st 2023 when I bought a BOB trailer in Myrtle Beach South Carolina. 

I tried the BOB for 1000 miles or better. Still have it in storage. Gave commentary on the channel. Of course, much more to say. 

Extreme minimalism is best, and very possible. Two wheels, mountain bike only is ideal for stealth lifestyle. Anything else adds complications. 

Tested and proven, for myself anyway. The more gear carried,  harder to get in and out of many places. Not worth it for me.

I sleep next to my bike and gear. With a trailer,  8 out of 10 places I sleep would be off limits. 

Try backing up out of any tight spot with a trailer. 

You are much more noticeable in public as transient with a trailer. 

So many disadvantages to experience with a trailer. 

A two wheel trailer would be a nightmare. 

Everything you carry must be contained in one tight mobile package.  

It is all about the choice you make about what to carry. Two rear stuff panniers are sufficient. Several packages are strapped to the bike, front rack, and handlebars, with velcro.

Compression stuff bags are essential.

This lifestyle is only attainable through understanding deep hidden time tested strategies.

It is one form of modern-era nomadic or semi-nomadic prepper-survivalism for those wanting to live and operate outside the system.

A big part is keeping all systems operational and ready to go at all times even when remaining stationary for a season or two, like a bug-out bag on wheels. 

While on the road, you must feel and listen to your bike at all times. Parts continually need replacement. 

Trailers complicate matters. Be stealth, lightweight, compact.

Concerning power consumption, one small efficient solar collector with 5v usb output plus one high capacity external battery pack is sufficient. The panel and battery can be a single unit.

Devices used should also have a strong efficient internal battery. All electronics should be usb rechargeable. 

When visiting or passing through civilization, in the US, there are often free and open power outlets in parks which can be used, and if you are minimalistic and efficient with your power consumption, you can get by without a solar collector and rely only on an external battery and random power outlet once or twice a week. 

I don't use cellular, which is a big power consumer, continuously operating in the background. Wifi and Bluetooth are always off unless specifically being used. I avoid Bluetooth as it also uses power in the background. Airplane mode is always on.
